audit.summary: Theorem1.12 has a false probability-density normalization, contradicted by the admissible one-particle case; its proof gives the corrected constant. Theorem4.1 cannot hold over its unrestricted p=k/n range. Theorem5.2 also omits a local factor1/2 that cancels in normalized correlation ratios. Fixed-p Theorem1.4 and the main Kasteleyn construction are not refuted by these checks.

proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:delta. A bead configuration on \(\mathbb T_n=[0,1)\times\mathbb Z_n\) has \(k\) beads on each string, neighboring strings interlace, and its occupation number is \(\ell\). The volume \(\operatorname{Vol}^{(n)}_{k,\ell}\) measures the corresponding ordered configurations. The empty case has separately defined weights \(\operatorname{Vol}^{(n)}_{0,\ell}=\binom n\ell\). The infinite-horizontal process has \(1\leq\ell\leq n-1\) particles, state \(E\subset\mathbb Z_n\), and \[
 \Delta(E)=\prod_{1\leq j<r\leq\ell}
 \left|e^{2\pi i h_r/n}-e^{2\pi i h_j/n}\right|,
 \qquad E=\{h_1,\ldots,h_\ell\}.\] An allowed jump replaces \(h\in E\) by \(h+1\notin E\), with addition modulo \(n\).

Representation: paraphrase

Location: Theorem1.12,p9; definitions and ratespp8-9; generators(6.21)-(6.22)p45; proof(6.26)-(6.27)p46

Text: The probability Radon-Nikodym derivative uses c=n_particle-(1/n)sin(pi*l/n)/sin(pi/n).

Integer n>=2 and1<=ell<=n-1. Both chains start from the same fixed configuration, as in the proof, or the same initial law. Allowed jumps are h->h+1 into a vacancy; Gordenko ratesDelta(E')/Delta(E),TASEP rates1.
